data.source_title: Clinical and cost implications of using immediate MRI in the management of patients with a suspected scaphoid fracture and negative radiographs: results from the SMaRT trial
data.locator: Abstract and Methods; randomized trial, initial MRI versus control follow-up.
data.source_setting: UK ED randomized trial; age at least 16, clinical history/exam consistent with suspected scaphoid fracture, negative initial four-view radiographs; exclusions included confirmed injury and out-of-catchment patients.
data.source_period: Published 2019; enrollment dates not stated in inspected abstract excerpt.
data.source_n: 136 randomized (68 per arm); 4 participants were lost to follow-up; analysis denominators at three months were 65 control and 67 intervention. Five intervention participants did not receive MRI.
data.quantity: Scaphoid fracture diagnosis by 3 months, MRI arm versus control
data.source_evidence_basis: Full-text Results report scaphoid fractures diagnosed up to three months: 4/65 control and 7/67 intervention (reported 6.2% and 10.4%). Five intervention participants did not undergo MRI; four participants withdrew and were lost to follow-up.
data.limitations: Randomized workflow comparison, not an untreated natural-history estimate. MRI-arm denominator requires caution because five randomized participants did not receive MRI; follow-up imaging differed by arm. Adult-only age threshold was 16, so population includes older adolescents.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only to compare trial pathway outcomes under its eligibility and follow-up process; do not interpret arm difference as causal probability for an individual or as local prevalence.
